1.pericope_label: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth: the gods of Babylon go into captivity on the backs of weary beasts
debates: Whether Bel and Nebo were deified men or gods of another kind
What the word rendered carriages means
How the inscription naming the conqueror as a worshipper of Bel is to be reconciled with the prophecy
outliers: Ellicott makes Bel a form of Marduk and Nabu an Assyrian Hermes, where Gill, Henry and Wesley all make them deified men
themes: Gods that must be carried by the beasts they were meant to protect
A conqueror who plunders temples for their metal
Idols reckoned as lumber rather than treasure
A prophecy dated by what it does not know

3.pericope_label: Hearken unto me: borne from the belly, carried to hoar hairs by the God who does not need carrying
debates: How far the figure of bearing from the womb may be pressed
Whether the emphatic word means simply he or means the same
Whether it is fitting that grown men should still need carrying
outliers: Calvin makes the image maternal where Clarke and Wesley make it that of a father and of parents generally
themes: A god carried against a God who carries
Care that outlasts the care of a mother
A remnant small enough that a hearing must be demanded of it
Grace measured from the womb rather than from merit

5.pericope_label: To whom will ye liken me: gold weighed out, a god hired from a goldsmith, and a procession that carries what cannot walk
debates: Whether the reproof reaches only those who worship wood and stone
What the word rendered show yourselves men means
Whether any likeness of God could lawfully be made
outliers: Calvin says many commentators absurdly weaken the passage by confining it to crude image-worship
themes: A god that must be fastened down so it can be found again
Two fathers of one idol, the purse and the workman
Covetousness reckoned the same sin indoors
Prosperity mistaken for divine approval

8.pericope_label: Remember this and shew yourselves men: the end declared from the beginning, and a ravenous bird called from the east
debates: What the word rendered shew yourselves men means
Whether the eighth verse addresses the Jews or the whole human race
Who the ravenous bird is, and whether the word means a bird at all
outliers: Calvin renders the word for the bird as thought or decree, against the greater part of interpreters and against his own admission that bird of prey is its true signification
Gill reports and rejects two older identifications of the bird, one making it Abraham and one Nebuchadnezzar
themes: A verb that appears once and cannot be pinned down
Memory prescribed as the cure for idolatry
A conqueror under the ensign of an eagle
Auguries answered by a bird nobody watched for

12.pericope_label: Hearken unto me, ye stouthearted: righteousness brought near, and salvation placed in Zion for Israel
debates: Whether far from righteousness means incapable of grace or abandoned to crime
What the righteousness brought near is
outliers: Clarke makes the stouthearted the Babylonians, a reading Gill attributes to Kimchi and rejects outright in favour of the Jews themselves
Gill takes the righteousness to be the imputed righteousness of Christ where Calvin and Wesley take it to be the promised deliverance
themes: A rebuke aimed at the afflicted rather than the comfortable
Unbelief as an obstacle that cannot finally obstruct
Salvation and glory tied in one knot
Nearness offered to men who will not come near
